title: Bob Lyons and Johnny Matoyas's place where the Zulus met
summary: She knows little of Bob Lyons; musicians gathered near Matoyas's place on Perdido Street where the Zulus met.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Do you remember anything else about Bob Lyons? He's dead now, but I thought we won't get to talk to him, of course. I wondered if you knew anything about his life.

No, I couldn't tell you nothing about Bob Lyons. All I know he used to be with Willie there, you know, play with him and all. But for me to have anything to say of him, I wouldn't know. I know he didn't worry with him too much, you know. My husband and them would be together with him. All the musicians used to be around there by Ruchacks. And used to be around there by Johnny Matoyas, where he's dead. You heard of him, eh? Certainly. When he died, Johnny Matoyas, he died. But he used to be there, because that's where them Zulus used to meet and that's where Willie and them used to play. Willie and them used to play for him. Warner could tell you that too, you know. He told you?
Where is Matoyas' place? He's all towed down.

He's all towed down there. Oh yeah, well that's where my husband and them used to go and they would play. They'd leave the horns all in my house, on the bed. Then they'd all go around there. When they'd get ready to start off playing, they'd all come back and get their horns. That was by Johnny Matoyas. He used to stay there, you see. That was where the Zulus used to have their meetings. Then they used to meet there.
Was that in the Air Ramport?

That was right in the block where Root Shack was on Padilla Street. Oh yeah, the same? Yeah, on the same side. Because, let me see, Root Shack was on the corner. And Johnny, and then they had a little, that cook shop like you say. And then Johnny Matoyas was right next door to that. But all that's towed down, that whole thing. So I'm going to go out there and get lost. I could get well now.
I think that Zulu is still in the pavement. The sidewalk still says Zulu Aid and Pages.
